claims.text: Rapidly quenched FeCoNiTi has a dual-phase microstructure comprising an fcc matrix and a hexagonal C14 Laves phase.
The fcc matrix in the dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy is ferromagnetic.
The dual-phase FeCoNiTi alloy exhibits multiple magnetic ordering transitions.
Coexistence with the C14 Laves phase enhances the coercivity of the fcc-containing FeCoNiTi alloy.
The Ti-rich C14 sublattice couples antiferromagnetically to Fe, Co, and Ni moments in the adjacent fcc phase.
Antiferromagnetic coupling to Ti suppresses the effective saturation magnetization of the fcc phase.
Ti atoms at the fcc/C14 interface possess localized magnetic moments.
The fcc/C14 phase boundaries act as strong magnetic-domain-wall pinning sites.
Interfacial antiferromagnetic coupling creates a high energy barrier for domain-wall motion.
Crystallographic mismatch between the fcc and C14 phases induces magnetic anisotropy that contributes to coercivity.
Varying C14 phase fraction and Ti concentration will modulate interfacial area and inter-sublattice exchange strength.
At 400 K, thermal energy overcomes minor anisotropy barriers without fully decoupling the proposed antiferromagnetic interaction.
The dual-phase alloy will exhibit a coercivity of approximately 667 Oe at 400 K.
A single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi baseline will have coercivity below or capped near 100 Oe.
The low coercivity of single-phase fcc FeCoNiTi is caused by insufficient orbital moments and absence of domain-wall pinning.
Saturation magnetization will decrease in proportion to the C14 phase fraction.
Effective coercivity enhancement requires a continuous, semi-continuous, or fine lamellar C14 morphology with high interfacial area.
Isolated large C14 precipitates will provide weaker pinning and insufficient coupling to alter the bulk magnetic ground state significantly.
A spin-polarized DFT supercell containing an fcc/C14 interface is proposed to calculate the fcc-region spin-resolved density of states at the Fermi level and the interfacial exchange energy.

The hypothesis is to be rejected if the dual-phase sample has coercivity below 200 Oe at 400 K, or if DFT predicts ferromagnetic or negligible Ti–matrix coupling, or if the interfacial fcc spin DOS is not reduced relative to the single-phase baseline.
